topic: Fully on-chain delivery of web apps (SSTORE2/3, EthFS v2, scripty v2, web3://, data: URI limits, sandboxing, EIP-7907/7954/8037, Fusaka/Glamsterdam/EOF status, L2 code-size limits, deployment cost, blobs)

findings.claim: EIP-7907 was removed from Fusaka at ACDE #216 on 2025-07-18 (14 votes for full removal vs 6 for a modified version); Fusaka shipped on mainnet 2025-12-03 (epoch 411,392) without it.
findings.relevance: Answers 'is EIP-7907 in Fusaka': no.

findings.claim: On 2026-09-29 EIP-7907 was rewritten (PR #12398) to defer size increases to EIP-7954 and keep only code-loading metering (24KB threshold, 2 gas per 32-byte word on cold load); status Draft; not in the Glamsterdam list.
findings.relevance: The size increase now lives in EIP-7954.

findings.claim: EIP-7954 raises max code size 24 KiB -> 64 KiB and initcode 48 KiB -> 128 KiB with no gas change; it is Scheduled for Inclusion in Glamsterdam (EIP-7773); Sepolia activates at epoch 353,024 = 2026-10-06 13:53:36 UTC; Hoodi/mainnet dates undecided.
findings.relevance: Chunk size can double after Glamsterdam; design chunker with a parameter.

findings.claim: EIP-8037 (State Creation Gas Cost Increase) is also SFI in Glamsterdam; CPSB = 1,530 gas/state byte; contract deployment cost rises ~8x for a 24 kB contract.
findings.relevance: Makes L1 deployment of 100-300 KB much more expensive post-Glamsterdam; favours Base.

findings.claim: EOF (EIP-7692) is absent from both the Fusaka meta (EIP-7607) and the Glamsterdam meta (EIP-7773) lists.
findings.relevance: Do not plan around EOF.

findings.claim: Fusaka (EIP-7607, Final) includes EIP-7825 per-transaction gas cap of 16,777,216 (2^24) and EIP-7935 default gas limit 60M.
findings.relevance: Caps how many SSTORE2 chunks fit per tx (3) and bounds view calls on some clients.

findings.claim: geth issue #35838 (2026-09-29): after Amsterdam/EIP-8037 the 2^24 cap is applied to eth_call (gasUsed exactly 16,777,216, out of gas) despite the 50M rpc.gascap default; issue open with PR #35845.
findings.relevance: tokenURI and every request() must fit under 16.7M gas.

findings.claim: geth --rpc.gascap default is 50,000,000 and --rpc.evmtimeout default 5s.
findings.relevance: Absolute ceiling for any view read.

findings.claim: ERC-5219 (Final) interface: request(string[] resource, KeyValue[] params) external view returns (uint16 statusCode, string body, KeyValue[] headers); ERC-6944 requires resolveMode() to return bytes32 '5219'.
findings.relevance: The on-chain HTTP surface for the token's website.

findings.claim: ERC-7617 adds a web3-next-chunk header for arbitrary-size content; ERC-7618 adds Content-Encoding gzip/br with gateway-side inflate; ERC-7774 adds Cache-Control: evm-events with a ClearPathCache event. All Draft.
findings.relevance: Lets large assets and compressed assets be served under the gas cap, with cache coherence.

findings.claim: ERC-6821 resolves web3:// ENS names via the 'contentcontract' text record, accepting 0x addresses or ERC-3770 chain-specific addresses, falling back to the ERC-137 address.
findings.relevance: web3://name.eth can point at a Base deployment.

findings.claim: w3link.io gateway format is https://<name>.<chainShortName>.w3link.io/<path> and lists Base mainnet (base/8453), Arbitrum One, Optimism and 20+ chains; Base Sepolia (84532) is not listed; w3eth.io is mainnet+ENS only.
findings.relevance: Zero-install https route to the token's site on Base; testnet needs a self-hosted gateway.

findings.claim: The Chrome web3:// extension (MV3) documents 'No support for wallet connections via window.ethereum'.
findings.relevance: Native-client wallet support is immature; gateways are the practical live origin.

findings.claim: MDN: Chromium and Firefox limit data: URLs to 512MB, Safari to 2048MB; top-level navigation to data: URLs is blocked in all modern browsers; data: URLs are unique opaque origins.
findings.relevance: Browser size limits never bind; opaque origin blocks wallet connection.

findings.claim: DecompressionStream is Baseline Widely available since May 2023 and accepts gzip, deflate, deflate-raw, brotli and zstd, with 'varying levels of support' for some formats (brotli/zstd reported Chromium-only by secondary sources).
findings.relevance: Native gzip inflate in the loader; brotli not yet cross-browser.

findings.claim: OpenSea: tokenURI may 'embed metadata onchain'; animation_url may be an HTML page where 'Scripts and relative paths within that page are supported, but browser extensions are not'; external media up to 300 MB; SVG cached as PNG.
findings.relevance: HTML NFTs render on OpenSea but cannot reach a wallet there.

findings.claim: MetaMask extension PR #46186 (opened 2026-09-04, Draft): frames with opaque origins (sandboxed iframes, CSP sandbox) still get window.ethereum injected but connection requests (eth_accounts, personal_sign) are refused.
findings.relevance: A data: document cannot sign; the live app needs a real origin.

findings.claim: Brave blocks window.ethereum in third-party iframes unless allow="ethereum", in first-party sandboxed iframes unless sandbox="allow-same-origin", and in data:/file: contexts (insecure).
findings.relevance: Confirms the opaque-origin rule across wallets.

findings.claim: Rainbow browser-extension issue #1616 (2024-07-04) 'window.ethereum not injected in iframes' remains open; MetaMask mobile issue #6200 (2023) on base64 data: URIs not rendering was closed as not planned.
findings.relevance: Wallet rendering/injection of on-chain HTML is inconsistent; keep a static SVG face.

findings.claim: Rarible and Rainbow current support for data:application/json tokenURIs and HTML animation_url could not be confirmed from primary documentation.
findings.relevance: Needs a device/marketplace matrix test.

findings.claim: Check Point (2021-10) showed an SVG with an iframe served on storage.opensea.io could reach window.ethereum; OpenSea fixed it within an hour of the 2021-09-26 report (primary research page not fetched).
findings.relevance: Why marketplaces sandbox animation_url.

findings.claim: Hübel (2022-01-27) demonstrated animation_url HTML executing arbitrary JS (IP detection) inside OpenSea's storefront iframe.
findings.relevance: Our page must self-impose CSP and never fetch externally.

findings.claim: IJIS paper (2024-09-17) shows embedded HTML in NFTs enables fingerprinting that links users to blockchain accounts on popular marketplaces.
findings.relevance: Privacy argument for default-src 'none' and no external connections.

findings.claim: SecureSign (arXiv 2511.14611, 2025-11-18) proposes a trusted parent emulating an EIP-6963 provider into a sandboxed iframe over postMessage.
findings.relevance: Pattern for the token's own web3:// shell to lend a wallet to its sandboxed data: artwork.

findings.claim: Solady SSTORE2 offers write (CREATE), writeCounterfactual (CREATE2), writeDeterministic (CREATE3, address depends only on salt), read with ranges; STOP-prefixed payload; max 65,534 bytes per pointer.
findings.relevance: Chunk store with identical addresses across chains; already sized for 64 KiB.

findings.claim: 0xsequence SSTORE2 benchmarks: 1,024 bytes write 245,522 gas (vs 732,080 SSTORE) and read 3,296 gas (vs 71,659 SLOAD); 24,576 bytes max per pointer.
findings.relevance: Justifies code-as-storage for the app bytes.

findings.claim: SSTORE3 stores data in storage then deploys via CREATE2 with constant init code so pointers can be small integers; better than SSTORE2 only when pointer packing saves slots and reads are frequent; reads slightly costlier.
findings.relevance: Irrelevant for 24 KB chunks; possible for per-token small published pages.

findings.claim: EthFS FileStore is at 0xFe1411d6864592549AdE050215482e4385dFa0FB on Ethereum, Sepolia, Holesky, Base, Base Sepolia, Optimism, OP Sepolia, Shape and Zora; files are lists of BytecodeSlice{pointer,start,end} written via Safe Singleton Factory in 24kb chunks; createFileFromSlices/Pointers/Chunks APIs.
findings.relevance: Public, content-addressed commons for our loader and libraries on Base.

findings.claim: scripty.sol v2: HTMLRequest{headTags,bodyTags}, HTMLTag{name,contractAddress,contractData,tagType,tagOpen,tagClose,tagContent}, HTMLTagType {useTagOpenAndClose, script, scriptBase64DataURI, scriptGZIPBase64DataURI, scriptPNGBase64DataURI}; ScriptyBuilderV2 at 0xD7587F110E08F4D120A231bA97d3B577A81Df022 on Ethereum, Sepolia, Holesky, Base, Base Sepolia, Optimism, OP Sepolia.
findings.relevance: Interoperability conventions (text/javascript+gzip); builder itself is heavier than a bespoke renderer.

findings.claim: Art Blocks Dependency Registry (0x37861f95882ACDba2cCD84F5bFc4598e2ECDDdAF) put p5.js v1.0.0 on chain in January 2024 as gzip chunks; the On-Chain Generator (0x953D288708bB771F969FCfD9BA0819eF506Ac718) assembles HTML from chain with scripty.sol.
findings.relevance: Leading project precedent for gzip+EthFS+scripty.

findings.claim: Base limits: ~400M gas per block, 2s blocks, per-tx max 16,777,216 (EIP-7825), min base fee 5,000,000 wei; code size not restated (EVM-equivalent, 24,576 inferred).
findings.relevance: Deployment batching and cost model on Base.

findings.claim: Base GasPriceOracle measured 2026-10-03 at block 52,098,952: baseFeeScalar 2,269; blobBaseFeeScalar 1,055,762; l1BaseFee 77,062,616 wei; blobBaseFee 4,809,132 wei; eth_gasPrice 6,000,000 wei.
findings.relevance: Inputs to the cost table (own RPC measurement).

findings.claim: Fjord L1 fee: estimatedSizeScaled = max(100e6, -42,585,600 + 836,500*fastlzSize); l1FeeScaled = baseFeeScalar*l1BaseFee*16 + blobFeeScalar*blobBaseFee; l1Fee = estimatedSizeScaled*l1FeeScaled/1e12.
findings.relevance: Cost math.

findings.claim: Computed: 300 KB in 13 SSTORE2 chunks ~69.8M gas; Base total ~0.00042 ETH (L1 data ~0.000002 ETH); mainnet 0.0105 ETH at 0.15 gwei to 0.349 ETH at 5 gwei; 100 KB: 0.000162 ETH Base / 0.004-0.134 ETH mainnet; at most 3 chunks per tx under the 2^24 cap.
findings.relevance: Deploy the app bytes on Base.

findings.claim: ethereum.org (2026-05-07): mainnet standard gas ~0.15 gwei with daily averages ~0.5 gwei; block gas limit 60M post-Fusaka with ~200M targeted post-Glamsterdam; blobs 6 target / 9 max.
findings.relevance: Mainnet cost assumptions.

findings.claim: Arbitrum One/Nova remain at 24KB; custom Arbitrum chains may set MaxCodeSize up to 96KB and MaxInitCodeSize up to 192KB at genesis, immutable afterwards; Stylus WASM must be <128KB uncompressed and <=24KB compressed.
findings.relevance: No public L2 offers a bigger code slot today.

findings.claim: EIP-7623 calldata floor (10 gas/token, tokens = zeros + 4*nonzeros) does not bind on SSTORE2 chunk deployment because the 200 gas/byte code deposit sits in the standard branch (983,040 floor vs 393,216 + 4,915,200 standard for 24,576 bytes).
findings.relevance: Chunk cost model.

findings.claim: EIP-4844 blobs are pruned after 4,096 epochs (~18 days); only the KZG commitment stays in the execution layer; long-term availability depends on third parties.
findings.relevance: Blobs are transport, not storage; secondary sources only, consistent with EIP-4844 spec.

findings.claim: IPSEITY (local repo) measured: 173,261 B document -> 113,379 B minified -> 39,501 B gzip in 3 shards; 21.65M gas to launch; tokenURI 19.99M gas / 103,808 B; ERC-5219 /live route 4.48M gas for the same page; plain-text storage would cost 23.58M gas to load.
findings.relevance: Real numbers for the two-surface design and the gas budget.

recommendations.recommendation: Ship two surfaces from one byte-stream: tokenURI (gzip data: URI, viewer) and an ERC-5219/6944 Premises serving the identical HTML at web3://<premises>:8453/token/<id>/live (plus /swap, /chat, /launch, /vault); prove byte equality in CI.
recommendations.rationale: data: documents have opaque origins; MetaMask (PR #46186), Brave and OpenSea ('browser extensions are not' supported) all block wallet use there. web3:// gives a real origin with no server; w3link.io already serves Base mainnet.

recommendations.recommendation: Budget every view call, tokenURI included, under 16,777,216 gas and gate CI on it; serve big assets with ERC-7617 chunks.
recommendations.rationale: EIP-7825 cap is live (Fusaka); geth #35838 shows the cap leaking into eth_call under Amsterdam; IPSEITY's 19.99M tokenURI already failed under it.

recommendations.recommendation: Store the document gzipped in SSTORE2 pointers and inflate with DecompressionStream('gzip') from a global-free loader; no brotli inside data:.
recommendations.rationale: Baseline since May 2023; saves ~62% load gas and ~77% bytes in IPSEITY's measurement; brotli decode is not cross-browser.

recommendations.recommendation: Use Solady SSTORE2.writeDeterministic (CREATE3) with fixed salts, freeze pointers one-way, and mirror the bytes into EthFS FileStore (0xFe1411…FB) via createFileFromSlices.
recommendations.rationale: Identical app addresses on every chain; content-addressed public commons; Solady already supports 65,534-byte pointers for EIP-7954.

recommendations.recommendation: Deploy the app bytes on Base (or another OP Stack chain) rather than mainnet.
recommendations.rationale: Measured ~0.00042 ETH for 300 KB on Base vs 0.0105-0.349 ETH on mainnet; EIP-8037 (Glamsterdam SFI) raises L1 deployment ~8x.

recommendations.recommendation: Self-impose CSP (<meta http-equiv=Content-Security-Policy content="default-src 'none'; …">), escape every chain string, no eval, no external src, no fetch beyond the user's RPC.
recommendations.rationale: The 2021 OpenSea SVG/iframe incident, the 2022 XSS demo and the 2024 fingerprinting paper are why marketplaces sandbox HTML; give them nothing.

recommendations.recommendation: Enforce holder/authorisation checks only in contracts; the page merely decides what to show from ownerOf/isApprovedForAll/ERC-6551/session keys.
recommendations.rationale: Reads are public on any chain; a page gate is a CSS class, a contract gate is enforcement.

recommendations.recommendation: Return Content-Type, Content-Encoding (ERC-7618) and Cache-Control: evm-events with ClearPathCache events (ERC-7774) from request().
recommendations.rationale: Gateways can cache aggressively yet refresh on swaps/messages; compressed assets stay under the gas cap.

recommendations.recommendation: Set the ENS contentcontract text record (ERC-6821) to an ERC-3770 value like base:0x… .
recommendations.rationale: web3://name.eth resolves straight to the Base deployment without IPFS or DNS.

recommendations.recommendation: Keep a small static SVG image face and ERC-7496 traits beside the HTML face.
recommendations.rationale: Wallets that never render HTML (MetaMask mobile history) still show the token; indexers avoid parsing a 100 KB URI.

recommendations.recommendation: Parameterise chunk size (24,576 now; 65,536 after EIP-7954 is live on the target chain) and verify both layouts in CI.
recommendations.rationale: 7954 is SFI for Glamsterdam (Sepolia 2026-10-06) but L2 adoption dates are unknown.

recommendations.recommendation: Expose /token/<id>/hash and an offline reconstruct script; publish the document hash in contractURI.
recommendations.rationale: Anyone with an RPC can rebuild and verify the page without trusting a gateway.

recommendations.recommendation: Offer brotli over ERC-7618 for gateway clients while keeping gzip for the data: path.
recommendations.rationale: Smaller bytes where the gateway inflates; no browser dependency.

recommendations.recommendation: Export non-canonical history (chat archives) to blobs/EthStorage only as a labelled convenience.
recommendations.rationale: Blobs are pruned after ~18 days; nothing the token's guarantees depend on may live there.

recommendations.recommendation: Do not use blobs, IPFS, external script src, upgradeable pointer tables, eval-based or brotli-only loaders, or reliance on marketplace iframes for signing.
recommendations.rationale: Each either breaks permanence, breaks under sandboxing, or reintroduces a trusted party.

special_ideas: Same web3:// origin on every chain via CREATE3-deterministic Premises and chunks (web3://0xSAME:1/, :8453/, :10/, :42161/), with ENS contentcontract pointing at the canonical chain.

A web3:// shell that hosts the token's own tokenURI artwork in a sandboxed iframe and lends it a wallet by emulating an EIP-6963 provider over postMessage (SecureSign pattern), so the marketplace-inert bytes become interactive inside the token's own site with parent-side confirmation.

Holder-published pages inside the token: /token/<id>/site serves bytes the holder wrote into their own SSTORE2/SSTORE3 pointer registered under the token's ERC-6551 account; transfers with the token; sealable.
First NFT to use ERC-7774 cache invalidation: emit ClearPathCache('/token/42/*') on every swap, message or launch so gateways serve fresh pages with HTTP cache semantics.

Capability-aware boot: opaque origin -> viewer with 'open live' link and QR; gateway https origin -> full app via EIP-6963; native web3:// -> full app plus deep links; 'zero' and 'no answer' always distinguished.
Terminal-verifiable integrity: web3curl /token/42/hash vs /token/42/raw; hash published in contractURI (ERC-7572).
Commons-first libraries: upload loader and shared JS to EthFS under versioned names with scripty-compatible text/javascript+gzip tags so Art Blocks/Alba/fxhash-style projects can reuse them.
Glamsterdam-ready chunker with a size parameter and CI proving identical output for 24,576 and 65,536-byte layouts.
/token/<id>/services.json machine route describing every capability so agents and wallets discover the swap/messaging/launchpad/vault without parsing HTML.
open_questions: Will Base/OP Stack adopt EIP-7954 (64 KiB) and EIP-8037 (8x deployment cost), and when?
Will MetaMask merge PR #46186 (refuse opaque-origin connections) and will other wallets follow; what is the exact failure mode to design UX copy around?
Do hosted RPCs (Alchemy, Infura, QuickNode, Base public endpoint) apply the 2^24 cap to eth_call today? Measure per provider before fixing the tokenURI budget.
Which wallets render HTML animation_url in 2026 (Rainbow, Rabby, Coinbase Wallet, MetaMask mobile)? No primary documentation found.
Does OpenSea still proxy animation_url HTML through its own storage domain, and with which sandbox flags?
Base Sepolia is absent from w3link.io: self-host web3url-gateway for testnet CI, or test on OP Sepolia/Sepolia?
When does DecompressionStream('brotli') reach Safari and Firefox?
EIP-7976 calldata floor numbers and whether it can ever bind on chunk deployment.
Is there an undocumented marketplace cap on data: metadata size? Only IPSEITY's 104 KB face is empirical evidence.
Which web3:// clients (Firefox add-on, Chrome extension, EVM Browser) actually implement ERC-7617/7618/7774 today?
